To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C‐terminal domain of the bacterial cell‐division membrane‐anchored FtsZ‐interacting protein ZipA is an RNA‐binding protein‐like fold, and the C‐terminal region of FtsZ interacts with the hydrophobic cavity of ZipA.

the ZipA domain has the split β‐β‐α fold found in several RNA‐binding proteins, that the ZipA–FtsZ complex has a β‐strand–α‐helix interface, that a small cluster of FtsZ residues are critical for binding to ZipA, and that ZipA is likely to be an RNA‐binding protein.
the ZipA C‐terminal fragment is a six‐β‐stranded β/α‐β domain and that the C‐terminus of FtsZ binds to this fragment as an extended β–α–β motif.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the interaction between ZipA and FtsZ.
the molecular mechanisms of bacterial cell division.
a new type of protein–protein interaction in which a β‐sheet of one partner binds an extended strand followed by an α‐helix of the second partner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZipA domain is an unusual protein that binds to a small β‐strand of FtsZ and that this binding is mediated by a hydrophobic cavity on the surface of the domain.
the ZipA–FtsZ interaction involves a hydrophobic groove of ZipA and an extended β‐sheet–helix segment in FtsZ, which is a unique mode of protein–protein recognition in prokaryotic cell division.
the FtsZ‐ZipA complex represents the first example of a bacterial protein‐protein complex that is stabilized by an extensive β‐strand–β‐sheet interface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FtsZ‐ZipA interaction involves a large hydrophobic surface on ZipA and a small hydrophobic patch on FtsZ.
the C‐terminal domain of ZipA binds to FtsA through its β‐sheet and to FtsZ through its α‐helices.

the ZipA–FtsZ interaction can be viewed as the formation of an antiparallel β‐sheet between the two proteins, and that the Zip‐A‐binding site on FtsZ is located at the interface between the FtsZ‐specific C‐terminal α‐helix and the β‐strand that follows the GTP‐binding domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZipA and FtsZ interact in an extended manner, with a β‐strand followed immediately by an α‐helix in FtsZ, and that this interaction occurs in a hydrophobic cavity on the surface of ZipA.
FtsZ binds to ZipA through a simple extended β‐strand–α‐helix motif that may represent a general binding mode for FtsZ.
ZipA and FtsZ bind in a manner reminiscent of protein–protein interactions that are mediated by RNA‐binding proteins.
